Performers
Hartford Symphony Orchestra (brass and percussion), Fritz Mahler (conductor) Documented

Both are credited on the Vanguard sleeve. Individual players are not identified.

[1] [2]
Work version
Original work for brass and percussion, composed in 1942 Documented

The sleeve identifies the standalone Fanfare, not an extract from Symphony No. 3. The edition and performing parts used are unknown.

[2] [4]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

1961 is the carrier publication year in the Archive catalogue, not a documented session year. Neither the consulted sleeve nor the item metadata establishes the session date.

[1] [2]
Place
Unknown Unknown

The ensemble’s name does not establish the recording venue.

[1] [2]
Label
Vanguard Stereolab Documented

Stereo vinyl LP; the sleeve describes Vanguard’s stereophonic recording and disc-cutting system.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
VSD-2085 Documented

The specific transferred US carrier is catalogued as a 1961 release.

[1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 2, band 1 Documented

Side and band follow the segmented filename and programme order. Matrix, take and stamper identifiers are unknown.

[3] [2]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP transfer Documented

Institutional transfer credit; no independently established personal mastering credit.

[1]
Transfer date
2021-09-20 Documented

From ripping_date 20210920231659. The August 2021 scan date and September 2021 upload date are separate events.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 with Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; segmented VBR MP3 derivative Documented

The item documents this transfer chain. Equalisation, pitch correction, noise reduction and additional restoration settings are unknown.

[1] [3]
Composition rights
Copyrighted Copland composition; permissions administered by Boosey & Hawkes for the Aaron Copland Fund for Music Documented

The Fund expressly states that Fanfare is not in the public domain. A phonogram term assessment does not clear the composition, an arrangement, or a modern score edition.

[4] [5] [6]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1961, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applies to the documented Vanguard carrier: its former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is not US or worldwide clearance, not a Creative Commons licence, and not a US-government recording. Composition rights remain separate.

[1] [2] [8] [7]

Aaron Copland, Fanfare for the Common Man; Hartford Symphony Orchestra, Fritz Mahler. Vanguard VSD-2085 (1961 issue), Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Copland composition remains copyrighted.
